name: t2d
title: Outpatient Management of Type 2 Diabetes
description: Older adult with previously controlled type 2 diabetes presents with worsening glycemic control, progressive complications, and caregiver burden. Covers diabetes management, complication screening, lifestyle counseling, and psychosocial assessment.
clinicalInvariants: Chief complaint: progressive fatigue and polydipsia over past 4-6 weeks in known T2D patient
Conditions: T2D (8 years, HbA1c rising from 7.1% to 8.2%), HTN (controlled), peripheral neuropathy, background retinopathy
Medications: metformin 1000mg BID, amlodipine 5mg daily, paracetamol PRN
Family history: mother with T2D and stroke, father with CAD, sister with T2D
Clinical findings: BP 138/82, BMI 27.8, dry mucous membranes, reduced monofilament sensation feet, diminished pedal pulses
Assessment: uncontrolled T2D, progressive neuropathy, background retinopathy, caregiver stress
Management: labs, consider GLP-1/SGLT2 add-on, glucometer provision, foot care, ophthalmology referral, depression screening, social work referral
Provider questions and SP responses remain substantively identical across all variants
